page: Amazon Web Services x8g.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance engineered around the 64-bit ARM architecture. Powered by custom AWS Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz, this Nitro-virtualized instance offers 16 physical cores configured with 1 thread per core, totaling 16 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration features 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 16.0 GB of RAM allocated per core. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 8 Gbps. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional throughput across memory-centric workloads. In synthetic tests, the instance registered a PassMark memory score of 3,097.48, placing it in the top 10% of evaluated configurations. Uncached memory bandwidth tests for large 256 MB blocks reached 292.71 GB/sec for read operations and 124.24 GB/sec for write operations, both ranking in the top 25%. In database operations, the instance achieved a PassMark database score of 23,817.9 and handled 32.54 million Redis SET operations per second. General multi-core compute capability is equally solid, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,156.0 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 27,303.55.

Tradeoffs on the x8g.4xlarge revolve around instruction-set characteristics and storage architecture. Because it utilizes the arm64 architecture, it lacks x86-specific vector extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX. Language model generation benchmarks reflect limitations on non-accelerated CPU hardware, delivering 18.4 tokens per second on a 135M model and 15.49 tokens per second on a 7B model. Furthermore, because local storage is absent, persistent disks must be provisioned over the network via EBS, sharing data pathways with standard application traffic.

Given its massive memory density and high uncached memory bandwidth, the AWS x8g.4xlarge offers strong qualitative cost efficiency for footprint-dense, memory-bound applications. The dedicated core topology eliminates hyperthreading contention, making the instance optimal for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis and Memcached deployments, distributed analytics, and enterprise data processing systems that demand high memory capacity per core without the cost overhead of hardware GPU acceleration.

With a 16:1 memory-to-core ratio, it provides 256.0 GB of RAM (16.0 GB per core) alongside a 36 MB L3 cache and 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no GPUs and no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the x8g.4xlarge demonstrates top-tier memory performance, achieving a PassMark memory score of 3,097.48 (top 10%) and large-block read bandwidth of 292.71 GB/sec (top 25%).
